+#!/usr/bin/env python3

+"""MTL: run a small pipeline DSL (filter/apply/group_by/window/aggregate) over a CSV of sales events."""

+

+import argparse

+import csv

+import io

+import json

+import math

+import re

+import sys

+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

+from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP, localcontext

+

+try:

+    from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo, ZoneInfoNotFoundError

+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover

+    ZoneInfo = None

+    ZoneInfoNotFoundError = Exception

+

+EXIT_CODES = {"bad_dsl": 1, "type_error": 2, "bad_io": 3, "runtime_error": 4}

+

+

+class MTLError(Exception):

+    def __init__(self, kind, message):

+        super().__init__(message)

+        self.kind = kind

+        self.message = message

+

+

+def dsl_error(msg):

+    return MTLError("bad_dsl", msg)

+

+

+def type_error(msg):

+    return MTLError("type_error", msg)

+

+

+def io_error(msg):

+    return MTLError("bad_io", msg)

+

+

+def runtime_error(msg):

+    return MTLError("runtime_error", msg)

+

+

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- types

+

+INT, FLOAT, STR, BOOL, TS = "int", "float", "string", "bool", "timestamp"

+NUMERIC = (INT, FLOAT)

+

+REQUIRED_COLUMNS = {

+    "timestamp": TS,

+    "location": STR,

+    "item": STR,

+    "price": FLOAT,

+    "quantity": FLOAT,

+    "unit": STR,

+    "category": STR,

+}

+

+EPOCH = datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

+ONE_US = timedelta(microseconds=1)

+

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- tokenizer

+

+TOKEN_RE = re.compile(

+    r"""

+    (?P<ws>\s+)

+  | (?P<num>(?:\d+\.\d*|\.\d+|\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)

+  | (?P<str>'[^'\n]*')

+  | (?P<ident>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)

+  | (?P<op><=|>=|==|!=|<|>|!|&|\||\+|-|\*|/|%|\(|\)|\[|\]|,)

+    """,

+    re.VERBOSE,

+)

+

+

+class Token:

+    __slots__ = ("kind", "value", "pos", "end")

+

+    def __init__(self, kind, value, pos, end):

+        self.kind = kind

+        self.value = value

+        self.pos = pos

+        self.end = end

+

+    def __repr__(self):

+        return f"{self.kind}:{self.value!r}"

+

+

+def tokenize(text):

+    tokens = []

+    pos = 0

+    while pos < len(text):

+        m = TOKEN_RE.match(text, pos)

+        if not m:

+            ch = text[pos]

+            if ch == "'":

+                raise dsl_error(f"unterminated string literal at column {pos + 1}")

+            raise dsl_error(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at column {pos + 1}")

+        kind = m.lastgroup

+        value = m.group()

+        if kind == "str":

+            if "\\" in value:

+                raise dsl_error("escape sequences are not allowed in string literals")

+            value = value[1:-1]

+        if kind != "ws":

+            tokens.append(Token(kind, value, m.start(), m.end()))

+        pos = m.end()

+    tokens.append(Token("eof", None, len(text), len(text)))

+    return tokens

+

+

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- AST

+

+class Lit:

+    def __init__(self, value, typ):

+        self.value = value

+        self.typ = typ

+

+

+class Col:

+    def __init__(self, name):

+        self.name = name

+

+

+class Call:

+    def __init__(self, name, args):

+        self.name = name

+        self.args = args

+

+

+class Unary:

+    def __init__(self, op, operand):

+        self.op = op

+        self.operand = operand

+

+

+class Binary:

+    def __init__(self, op, left, right):

+        self.op = op

+        self.left = left

+        self.right = right

+

+

+FUNCTION_ARITY = {"len": (1, 1), "day": (1, 1), "month": (1, 1), "year": (1, 1), "round": (1, 2)}

+AGG_FUNCTIONS = ("average", "median", "sum", "count", "std", "var", "min", "max")

+COMPARISON_OPS = ("<", "<=", ">", ">=", "==", "!=")

+STATEMENT_KEYWORDS = ("filter", "apply", "group_by", "window", "aggregate")

+

+

+class Parser:

+    def __init__(self, text):

+        self.tokens = tokenize(text)

+        self.i = 0

+

+    # -- helpers

+    def peek(self, offset=0):

+        return self.tokens[min(self.i + offset, len(self.tokens) - 1)]

+

+    def next(self):

+        tok = self.tokens[self.i]

+        if tok.kind != "eof":

+            self.i += 1

+        return tok

+

+    def at(self, kind, value=None):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        return tok.kind == kind and (value is None or tok.value == value)

+

+    def at_op(self, *values):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        return tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in values

+

+    def expect_op(self, value):

+        tok = self.next()

+        if tok.kind != "op" or tok.value != value:

+            raise dsl_error(f"expected '{value}' but found {describe(tok)}")

+        return tok

+

+    def expect_ident(self, what="identifier"):

+        tok = self.next()

+        if tok.kind != "ident":

+            raise dsl_error(f"expected {what} but found {describe(tok)}")

+        return tok.value

+

+    def expect_eof(self):

+        tok = self.peek()

+        if tok.kind != "eof":

+            raise dsl_error(f"unexpected {describe(tok)} at end of statement")

+

+    # -- expressions

+    def parse_expr(self):

+        return self.parse_or()

+

+    def parse_or(self):

+        node = self.parse_and()

+        while self.at_op("|"):

+            self.next()

+            node = Binary("|", node, self.parse_and())

+        return node

+

+    def parse_and(self):

+        node = self.parse_not()

+        while self.at_op("&"):

+            self.next()

+            node = Binary("&", node, self.parse_not())

+        return node

+

+    def parse_not(self):

+        if self.at_op("!"):

+            self.next()

+            return Unary("!", self.parse_not())

+        return self.parse_comparison()

+

+    def parse_comparison(self):

+        node = self.parse_additive()

+        if self.at_op(*COMPARISON_OPS):

+            op = self.next().value

+            node = Binary(op, node, self.parse_additive())

+        elif self.at("ident", "in"):

+            self.next()

+            node = Binary("in", node, self.parse_additive())

+        else:

+            return node

+        if self.at_op(*COMPARISON_OPS) or self.at("ident", "in"):

+            raise dsl_error("comparison operators cannot be chained; use parentheses")

+        return node

+

+    def parse_additive(self):

+        node = self.parse_multiplicative()

+        while self.at_op("+", "-"):

+            op = self.next().value

+            node = Binary(op, node, self.parse_multiplicative())

+        return node

+

+    def parse_multiplicative(self):

+        node = self.parse_unary()

+        while self.at_op("*", "/", "%"):

+            op = self.next().value

+            node = Binary(op, node, self.parse_unary())

+        return node

+

+    def parse_unary(self):

+        if self.at_op("-", "+"):

+            op = self.next().value

+            operand = self.parse_unary()

+            if isinstance(operand, Lit) and operand.typ in NUMERIC:

+                return Lit(-operand.value if op == "-" else operand.value, operand.typ)

+            return operand if op == "+" else Unary("-", operand)

+        return self.parse_primary()

+

+    def parse_primary(self):

+        tok = self.next()

+        if tok.kind == "num":

+            if re.fullmatch(r"\d+", tok.value):

+                return Lit(int(tok.value), INT)

+            value = float(tok.value)

+            if not math.isfinite(value):

+                raise dsl_error(f"numeric literal {tok.value} is out of range")

+            return Lit(value, FLOAT)

+        if tok.kind == "str":

+            return Lit(tok.value, STR)

+        if tok.kind == "ident":

+            if tok.value == "true":

+                return Lit(True, BOOL)

+            if tok.value == "false":

+                return Lit(False, BOOL)

+            if tok.value == "in":

+                raise dsl_error("unexpected keyword 'in'")

+            if self.at_op("("):

+                return self.parse_call(tok.value)

+            return Col(tok.value)

+        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == "(":

+            node = self.parse_expr()

+            self.expect_op(")")

+            return node

+        raise dsl_error(f"unexpected {describe(tok)} in expression")

+

+    def parse_call(self, name):

+        if name not in FUNCTION_ARITY:

+            raise dsl_error(f"unknown function '{name}'")

+        self.expect_op("(")

+        args = []

+        if not self.at_op(")"):

+            args.append(self.parse_expr())

+            while self.at_op(","):

+                self.next()

+                args.append(self.parse_expr())

+        self.expect_op(")")

+        lo, hi = FUNCTION_ARITY[name]

+        if not lo <= len(args) <= hi:

+            expected = str(lo) if lo == hi else f"{lo} to {hi}"

+            raise dsl_error(f"function '{name}' expects {expected} argument(s), got {len(args)}")

+        return Call(name, args)

+

+

+def describe(tok):

+    if tok.kind == "eof":

+        return "end of statement"

+    if tok.kind == "str":

+        return f"string '{tok.value}'"

+    return f"'{tok.value}'"

+

+

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- statements

+

+class Program:

+    def __init__(self):

+        self.steps = []  # ("filter", expr) | ("apply", expr, name)

+        self.group_by = None  # list of column names

+        self.window = None  # width in microseconds

+        self.window_text = None

+        self.aggregates = None  # list of (fn, column-or-None, alias)

+

+

+def split_statements(text):

+    """Strip comments and join physical lines into logical statements."""

+    statements = []

+    buf = []

+    depth = 0

+    start_line = None

+    for lineno, raw in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):

+        out = []

+        in_str = False

+        for ch in raw:

+            if in_str:

+                if ch == "'":

+                    in_str = False

+            elif ch == "'":

+                in_str = True

+            elif ch == "#":

+                break

+            elif ch in "([":

+                depth += 1

+            elif ch in ")]":

+                depth -= 1

+            out.append(ch)

+        line = "".join(out).strip()

+        if not line and not buf:

+            continue

+        if not buf:

+            start_line = lineno

+        if line:

+            buf.append(line)

+        joined = " ".join(buf)

+        if depth > 0 or joined.endswith(",") or joined == "aggregate":

+            continue

+        statements.append((start_line, joined))

+        buf = []

+        depth = 0

+    if buf:

+        statements.append((start_line, " ".join(buf)))

+    return statements

+

+

+DURATION_UNITS = {"m": 60, "h": 3600, "d": 86400}

+

+

+def parse_program(text):

+    program = Program()

+    for lineno, stmt in split_statements(text):

+        try:

+            parse_statement(program, stmt)

+        except MTLError as e:

+            if e.kind == "bad_dsl":

+                raise dsl_error(f"line {lineno}: {e.message}")

+            raise

+    if program.aggregates is None:

+        raise dsl_error("exactly one 'aggregate' statement is required")

+    validate_output_keys(program)

+    return program

+

+

+def parse_statement(program, stmt):

+    p = Parser(stmt)

+    head = p.next()

+    if head.kind != "ident" or head.value not in STATEMENT_KEYWORDS:

+        raise dsl_error(f"unknown statement starting with {describe(head)}")

+    kw = head.value

+    if kw == "filter":

+        p.expect_op("(")

+        expr = p.parse_expr()

+        p.expect_op(")")

+        p.expect_eof()

+        program.steps.append(("filter", expr))

+    elif kw == "apply":

+        p.expect_op("(")

+        expr = p.parse_expr()

+        p.expect_op(",")

+        name = p.expect_ident("new column name")

+        if name in ("true", "false", "in"):

+            raise dsl_error(f"'{name}' is a reserved word and cannot be a column name")

+        p.expect_op(")")

+        p.expect_eof()

+        program.steps.append(("apply", expr, name))

+    elif kw == "group_by":

+        if program.group_by is not None:

+            raise dsl_error("at most one 'group_by' statement is allowed")

+        p.expect_op("(")

+        cols = []

+        if p.at_op("["):

+            p.next()

+            cols.append(p.expect_ident("column name"))

+            while p.at_op(","):

+                p.next()

+                cols.append(p.expect_ident("column name"))

+            p.expect_op("]")

+        else:

+            cols.append(p.expect_ident("column name"))

+        p.expect_op(")")

+        p.expect_eof()

+        if len(set(cols)) != len(cols):

+            raise dsl_error("duplicate column in group_by")

+        program.group_by = cols

+    elif kw == "window":

+        if program.window is not None:

+            raise dsl_error("at most one 'window' statement is allowed")

+        p.expect_op("(")

+        num = p.next()

+        unit = p.next()

+        if (

+            num.kind != "num"

+            or not re.fullmatch(r"\d+", num.value)

+            or unit.kind != "ident"

+            or unit.value not in DURATION_UNITS

+            or unit.pos != num.end

+        ):

+            raise dsl_error("invalid duration literal; expected e.g. 10m, 1h, 7d")

+        p.expect_op(")")

+        p.expect_eof()

+        amount = int(num.value)

+        if amount <= 0:

+            raise dsl_error("window duration must be positive")

+        program.window = amount * DURATION_UNITS[unit.value] * 1_000_000

+        program.window_text = num.value + unit.value

+    elif kw == "aggregate":

+        if program.aggregates is not None:

+            raise dsl_error("exactly one 'aggregate' statement is required")

+        aggs = [parse_agg_entry(p)]

+        while p.at_op(","):

+            p.next()

+            aggs.append(parse_agg_entry(p))

+        p.expect_eof()

+        aliases = [a[2] for a in aggs]

+        dup = sorted({a for a in aliases if aliases.count(a) > 1})

+        if dup:

+            raise dsl_error(f"duplicate aggregate alias '{dup[0]}'")

+        program.aggregates = aggs

+

+

+def parse_agg_entry(p):

+    fn = p.expect_ident("aggregate function")

+    if fn not in AGG_FUNCTIONS:

+        raise dsl_error(f"unknown aggregate function '{fn}'")

+    p.expect_op("(")

+    if p.at_op("*"):

+        p.next()

+        col = None

+    else:

+        col = p.expect_ident("column name or '*'")

+    p.expect_op(")")

+    if not p.at("ident", "as"):

+        raise dsl_error(f"expected 'as <alias>' after {fn}(...), found {describe(p.peek())}")

+    p.next()

+    alias = p.expect_ident("alias")

+    return (fn, col, alias)

+

+

+def validate_output_keys(program):

+    reserved = set(program.group_by or [])

+    if program.window is not None:

+        for key in ("window_start", "window_end"):

+            if key in reserved:

+                raise dsl_error(f"group_by column '{key}' collides with window output field")

+            reserved.add(key)

+    for _, _, alias in program.aggregates:

+        if alias in reserved:

+            raise dsl_error(f"aggregate alias '{alias}' collides with another output field")

+

+

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- CSV loading

+

+NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"[+-]?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?|[+-]?(?:inf|infinity|nan)", re.IGNORECASE)

+INT_RE = re.compile(r"[+-]?\d+")

+

+

+def parse_number(s):

+    s = s.strip()

+    if not NUMBER_RE.fullmatch(s):

+        raise ValueError(s)

+    return float(s)

+

+

+def make_ts_parser(tz, fmt):

+    def parse(s):

+        s = s.strip()

+        if fmt:

+            dt = datetime.strptime(s, fmt)

+        else:

+            t = s[:-1] + "+00:00" if s[-1:] in ("Z", "z") else s

+            dt = datetime.fromisoformat(t)

+        if dt.tzinfo is None:

+            dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=tz)

+        return dt.astimezone(timezone.utc)

+

+    return parse

+

+

+def infer_type(values, parse_ts):

+    present = [v.strip() for v in values if v.strip() != ""]

+    if not present:

+        return STR

+    if all(INT_RE.fullmatch(v) for v in present):

+        return INT

+    if all(NUMBER_RE.fullmatch(v) for v in present):

+        return FLOAT

+    if all(v.lower() in ("true", "false") for v in present):

+        return BOOL

+    if all(":" in v for v in present):

+        try:

+            for v in present:

+                parse_ts(v)

+            return TS

+        except (ValueError, OverflowError):

+            pass

+    return STR

+

+

+def convert(value, typ, parse_ts):

+    if typ == STR:

+        return value

+    v = value.strip()

+    if v == "":

+        return None

+    if typ == FLOAT:

+        return parse_number(v)

+    if typ == INT:

+        return int(v)

+    if typ == BOOL:

+        low = v.lower()

+        if low not in ("true", "false"):

+            raise ValueError(v)

+        return low == "true"

+    return parse_ts(v)

+

+

+def load_csv(path, parse_ts):

+    try:

+        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:

+            data = f.read()

+    except FileNotFoundError:

+        raise io_error(f"CSV file not found: {path}")

+    except IsADirectoryError:

+        raise io_error(f"CSV path is a directory: {path}")

+    except UnicodeDecodeError:

+        raise io_error(f"CSV file is not valid UTF-8: {path}")

+    except OSError as e:

+        raise io_error(f"cannot read CSV file {path}: {e.strerror or e}")

+    try:

+        records = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(data, newline="")))

+    except csv.Error as e:

+        raise io_error(f"malformed CSV: {e}")

+    if not records:

+        raise io_error("CSV file is empty; a header row is required")

+    header = [h.strip() for h in records[0]]

+    if len(set(header)) != len(header):

+        raise io_error("CSV header contains duplicate column names")

+    missing = [c for c in REQUIRED_COLUMNS if c not in header]

+    if missing:

+        raise io_error(f"CSV is missing required column(s): {', '.join(missing)}")

+    body = []

+    for lineno, rec in enumerate(records[1:], 2):

+        if not rec or (len(rec) == 1 and rec[0].strip() == ""):

+            continue

+        if len(rec) != len(header):

+            raise io_error(f"CSV row {lineno} has {len(rec)} fields, expected {len(header)}")

+        body.append(rec)

+

+    schema = {}

+    columns = {}

+    for idx, name in enumerate(header):

+        raw = [rec[idx] for rec in body]

+        typ = REQUIRED_COLUMNS.get(name) or infer_type(raw, parse_ts)

+        schema[name] = typ

+        converted = []

+        for offset, value in enumerate(raw):

+            try:

+                converted.append(convert(value, typ, parse_ts))

+            except (ValueError, OverflowError):

+                raise type_error(f"column '{name}' has invalid {typ} value {value!r}")

+        columns[name] = converted

+    rows = [{name: columns[name][i] for name in header} for i in range(len(body))]

+    return schema, rows

+

+

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- compile (type check + evaluator)

+

+def type_name(t):

+    return "number" if t in NUMERIC else t

+

+

+def check_finite(x):

+    if isinstance(x, float) and not math.isfinite(x):

+        raise runtime_error("expression produced a non-finite number")

+    return x

+

+

+def round_half_away(x, digits):

+    if isinstance(x, int) and digits >= 0:

+        return x

+    if isinstance(x, float) and not math.isfinite(x):

+        raise runtime_error("cannot round a non-finite number")

+    if digits > 400:

+        return x

+    if digits < -400:

+        return 0 if isinstance(x, int) else 0.0

+    with localcontext() as ctx:

+        ctx.prec = 1000

+        try:

+            d = Decimal(repr(x)).quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-digits), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

+        except InvalidOperation:

+            raise runtime_error("round() failed")

+    if isinstance(x, int):

+        return int(d)

+    result = float(d)

+    if result == 0:

+        result = 0.0

+    return check_finite(result)

+

+

+def arith(op, a, b):

+    try:

+        if op == "+":

+            r = a + b

+        elif op == "-":

+            r = a - b

+        elif op == "*":

+            r = a * b

+        elif op == "/":

+            if b == 0:

+                raise runtime_error("division by zero")

+            r = a / b

+        else:

+            if b == 0:

+                raise runtime_error("modulo by zero")

+            r = a % b

+    except OverflowError:

+        raise runtime_error("numeric overflow")

+    return check_finite(r)

+

+

+COMPARE = {

+    "<": lambda a, b: a < b,

+    "<=": lambda a, b: a <= b,

+    ">": lambda a, b: a > b,

+    ">=": lambda a, b: a >= b,

+    "==": lambda a, b: a == b,

+    "!=": lambda a, b: a != b,

+}

+

+

+def compile_expr(node, schema, tz):

+    """Type-check `node` against `schema`; return (type, evaluator(row))."""

+    if isinstance(node, Lit):

+        value = node.value

+        return node.typ, lambda row: value

+

+    if isinstance(node, Col):

+        if node.name not in schema:

+            raise type_error(f"unknown column '{node.name}'")

+        name = node.name

+        return schema[name], lambda row: row[name]

+

+    if isinstance(node, Unary):

+        t, f = compile_expr(node.operand, schema, tz)

+        if node.op == "!":

+            if t != BOOL:

+                raise type_error(f"'!' requires a boolean operand, got {type_name(t)}")

+            return BOOL, lambda row: not f(row)

+        if t not in NUMERIC:

+            raise type_error(f"unary '-' requires a numeric operand, got {type_name(t)}")

+

+        def neg(row):

+            v = f(row)

+            return None if v is None else -v

+

+        return t, neg

+

+    if isinstance(node, Call):

+        return compile_call(node, schema, tz)

+

+    op = node.op

+    if op == "in":

+        if not (isinstance(node.left, Lit) and node.left.typ == STR):

+            raise type_error("'in' requires a string literal on the left (<string_literal> in <string_col>)")

+        if not isinstance(node.right, Col):

+            raise type_error("'in' requires a string column on the right (<string_literal> in <string_col>)")

+        rt, rf = compile_expr(node.right, schema, tz)

+        if rt != STR:

+            raise type_error(f"'in' requires a string column on the right, column '{node.right.name}' is {type_name(rt)}")

+        needle = node.left.value

+

+        def contains(row):

+            v = rf(row)

+            return v is not None and needle in v

+

+        return BOOL, contains

+

+    lt, lf = compile_expr(node.left, schema, tz)

+    rt, rf = compile_expr(node.right, schema, tz)

+

+    if op in ("&", "|"):

+        if lt != BOOL or rt != BOOL:

+            raise type_error(f"'{op}' requires boolean operands, got {type_name(lt)} and {type_name(rt)}")

+        if op == "&":

+            return BOOL, lambda row: bool(lf(row)) and bool(rf(row))

+        return BOOL, lambda row: bool(lf(row)) or bool(rf(row))

+

+    if op in COMPARISON_OPS:

+        ok = (

+            (lt in NUMERIC and rt in NUMERIC)

+            or (lt == rt and lt in (STR, TS))

+            or (lt == rt == BOOL and op in ("==", "!="))

+        )

+        if not ok:

+            raise type_error(f"cannot compare {type_name(lt)} with {type_name(rt)} using '{op}'")

+        cmp = COMPARE[op]

+

+        def compare(row):

+            a = lf(row)

+            if a is None:

+                return False

+            b = rf(row)

+            if b is None:

+                return False

+            return cmp(a, b)

+

+        return BOOL, compare

+

+    # arithmetic

+    if lt not in NUMERIC or rt not in NUMERIC:

+        raise type_error(f"'{op}' requires numeric operands, got {type_name(lt)} and {type_name(rt)}")

+    result_type = FLOAT if op == "/" or FLOAT in (lt, rt) else INT

+

+    def evaluate(row):

+        a = lf(row)

+        if a is None:

+            return None

+        b = rf(row)

+        if b is None:

+            return None

+        return arith(op, a, b)

+

+    return result_type, evaluate

+

+

+def compile_call(node, schema, tz):

+    name = node.name

+    compiled = [compile_expr(a, schema, tz) for a in node.args]

+    t, f = compiled[0]

+    if name == "len":

+        if t != STR:

+            raise type_error(f"len() requires a string argument, got {type_name(t)}")

+

+        def length(row):

+            v = f(row)

+            return None if v is None else len(v)

+

+        return INT, length

+    if name in ("day", "month", "year"):

+        if t != TS:

+            raise type_error(f"{name}() requires a timestamp argument, got {type_name(t)}")

+        attr = name

+

+        def part(row):

+            v = f(row)

+            return None if v is None else getattr(v.astimezone(tz), attr)

+

+        return INT, part

+    # round

+    if t not in NUMERIC:

+        raise type_error(f"round() requires a numeric argument, got {type_name(t)}")

+    if len(compiled) == 2:

+        dt, df = compiled[1]

+        if dt != INT:

+            raise type_error(f"round() digits must be an integer, got {type_name(dt)}")

+    else:

+        df = lambda row: 0  # noqa: E731

+

+    def rounder(row):

+        v = f(row)

+        if v is None:

+            return None

+        d = df(row)

+        if d is None:

+            return None

+        return round_half_away(v, d)

+

+    return t, rounder

+

+

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- aggregation

+

+def agg_sum(vals):

+    try:

+        total = 0

+        for v in vals:

+            total += v

+    except OverflowError:

+        raise runtime_error("numeric overflow in sum")

+    return total

+

+

+def agg_mean(vals):

+    return agg_sum(vals) / len(vals)

+

+

+def agg_var(vals):

+    mean = agg_mean(vals)

+    acc = 0.0

+    for v in vals:

+        d = v - mean

+        acc += d * d

+    return acc / len(vals)

+

+

+def agg_median(vals):

+    s = sorted(vals)

+    n = len(s)

+    mid = n // 2

+    if n % 2:

+        return s[mid]

+    return (s[mid - 1] + s[mid]) / 2

+

+

+AGG_IMPL = {

+    "sum": agg_sum,

+    "average": agg_mean,

+    "median": agg_median,

+    "var": agg_var,

+    "std": lambda vals: math.sqrt(check_finite(agg_var(vals))),

+    "min": min,

+    "max": max,

+}

+

+

+def compute_aggregate(fn, col, rows):

+    if col is None:

+        return len(rows)

+    vals = [r[col] for r in rows if r[col] is not None]

+    if fn == "count":

+        return len(vals)

+    if any(isinstance(v, float) and math.isnan(v) for v in vals):

+        raise runtime_error(f"{fn}({col}) produced a non-finite number")

+    if not vals:

+        return None

+    try:

+        result = AGG_IMPL[fn](vals)

+    except OverflowError:

+        raise runtime_error(f"numeric overflow in {fn}({col})")

+    if isinstance(result, float) and not math.isfinite(result):

+        raise runtime_error(f"{fn}({col}) produced a non-finite number")

+    return result

+

+

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- execution

+

+def format_ts(dt):

+    dt = dt.astimezone(timezone.utc)

+    s = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")

+    if dt.microsecond:

+        s += f".{dt.microsecond:06d}"

+    return s + "Z"

+

+

+def to_json_value(v):

+    if isinstance(v, datetime):

+        return format_ts(v)

+    if isinstance(v, float):

+        if not math.isfinite(v):

+            raise runtime_error("result contains a non-finite number")

+        return 0.0 if v == 0 else v

+    return v

+

+

+def sort_key(value):

+    if value is None:

+        return (0, 0)

+    return (1, value)

+

+

+def run(program, schema, rows, tz):

+    schema = dict(schema)

+    compiled_steps = []

+    for step in program.steps:

+        t, f = compile_expr(step[1], schema, tz)

+        if step[0] == "filter":

+            if t != BOOL:

+                raise type_error(f"filter expression must be boolean, got {type_name(t)}")

+            compiled_steps.append(("filter", f, None))

+        else:

+            schema[step[2]] = t

+            compiled_steps.append(("apply", f, step[2]))

+

+    group_cols = program.group_by or []

+    for c in group_cols:

+        if c not in schema:

+            raise type_error(f"unknown group_by column '{c}'")

+    if program.window is not None:

+        if schema.get("timestamp") != TS:

+            raise type_error("window requires 'timestamp' to be a timestamp column")

+    for fn, col, alias in program.aggregates:

+        if col is None:

+            if fn != "count":

+                raise type_error(f"{fn}(*) is not allowed; only count(*) accepts '*'")

+            continue

+        if col not in schema:

+            raise type_error(f"unknown column '{col}' in {fn}({col})")

+        if schema[col] not in NUMERIC:

+            raise type_error(f"{fn}({col}) requires a numeric column, '{col}' is {type_name(schema[col])}")

+

+    for kind, f, name in compiled_steps:

+        if kind == "filter":

+            rows = [r for r in rows if f(r)]

+        else:

+            for r in rows:

+                r[name] = f(r)

+

+    windowed = program.window is not None

+    if not windowed and not group_cols:

+        out = {}

+        for fn, col, alias in sorted(program.aggregates, key=lambda a: a[2]):

+            out[alias] = to_json_value(compute_aggregate(fn, col, rows))

+        return out

+

+    buckets = {}

+    width = program.window

+    for r in rows:

+        if windowed:

+            ts = r["timestamp"]

+            if ts is None:

+                continue

+            us = (ts - EPOCH) // ONE_US

+            start = (us // width) * width

+        else:

+            start = None

+        key = (start, tuple(r[c] for c in group_cols))

+        buckets.setdefault(key, []).append(r)

+

+    def bucket_order(key):

+        start, gvals = key

+        return (start if start is not None else 0, tuple(sort_key(v) for v in gvals))

+

+    result = []

+    for key in sorted(buckets, key=bucket_order):

+        start, gvals = key

+        members = buckets[key]

+        obj = {}

+        if windowed:

+            obj["window_start"] = format_ts(EPOCH + timedelta(microseconds=start))

+            obj["window_end"] = format_ts(EPOCH + timedelta(microseconds=start + width))

+        for c, v in zip(group_cols, gvals):

+            obj[c] = to_json_value(v)

+        for fn, col, alias in sorted(program.aggregates, key=lambda a: a[2]):

+            obj[alias] = to_json_value(compute_aggregate(fn, col, members))

+        result.append(obj)

+    return result

+

+

+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- CLI

+

+class ArgParser(argparse.ArgumentParser):

+    def error(self, message):

+        raise io_error(f"invalid arguments: {message}")

+

+

+def resolve_tz(name):

+    if name in ("UTC", "Z", "Etc/UTC"):

+        return timezone.utc

+    if ZoneInfo is None:

+        raise io_error(f"timezone support unavailable for '{name}'")

+    try:

+        return ZoneInfo(name)

+    except (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError, OSError):

+        raise io_error(f"unknown timezone '{name}'")

+

+

+def read_dsl(path):

+    if path == "-":

+        try:

+            return sys.stdin.read()

+        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:

+            raise io_error(f"cannot read DSL from STDIN: {e}")

+    try:

+        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:

+            return f.read()

+    except FileNotFoundError:

+        raise io_error(f"DSL file not found: {path}")

+    except IsADirectoryError:

+        raise io_error(f"DSL path is a directory: {path}")

+    except UnicodeDecodeError:

+        raise io_error(f"DSL file is not valid UTF-8: {path}")

+    except OSError as e:

+        raise io_error(f"cannot read DSL file {path}: {e.strerror or e}")

+

+

+def main(argv=None):

+    parser = ArgParser(prog="mtl.py", description="Run an MTL pipeline over a CSV of sales events.")

+    parser.add_argument("--csv", required=True)

+    parser.add_argument("--dsl", required=True)

+    parser.add_argument("--out", default=None)

+    parser.add_argument("--tz", default="UTC")

+    parser.add_argument("--timestamp-format", dest="timestamp_format", default=None)

+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

+

+    tz = resolve_tz(args.tz)

+    program = parse_program(read_dsl(args.dsl))

+    schema, rows = load_csv(args.csv, make_ts_parser(tz, args.timestamp_format))

+    result = run(program, schema, rows, tz)

+    try:

+        text = json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False) + "\n"

+    except ValueError:

+        raise runtime_error("result contains a non-finite number")

+

+    if args.out and args.out != "-":

+        try:

+            with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

+                f.write(text)

+        except OSError as e:

+            raise io_error(f"cannot write output file {args.out}: {e.strerror or e}")

+    else:

+        sys.stdout.write(text)

+        sys.stdout.flush()

+    return 0

+

+

+def entry():

+    try:

+        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")

+    except (AttributeError, ValueError):

+        pass

+    try:

+        code = main()

+    except MTLError as e:

+        msg = " ".join(str(e.message).split())

+        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR:{e.kind}:{msg}\n")

+        code = EXIT_CODES[e.kind]

+    except RecursionError:

+        sys.stderr.write("ERROR:bad_dsl:expression is nested too deeply\n")

+        code = 1

+    except Exception as e:  # unexpected failure during execution

+        msg = " ".join(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}".split())

+        sys.stderr.write(f"ERROR:runtime_error:{msg}\n")

+        code = 4

+    sys.exit(code)

+

+

+if __name__ == "__main__":

+    entry()

+# MTL — design plan

+

+Single-file CLI `mtl.py` (stdlib only; `tzdata` in `requirements.txt` so IANA zones

+resolve on systems without a system tz database).

+

+## Pipeline of the program

+

+1. **CLI** (`argparse`, with usage errors mapped to `ERROR:bad_io:` / exit 3).

+2. **Read DSL** (file or STDIN) → I/O errors exit 3.

+3. **Parse DSL** → `Program(steps=[filter|apply...], group_by, window, aggregates)`.

+   Syntax errors exit 1.

+4. **Load CSV** → header + rows, typed columns. Missing file / bad encoding /

+   ragged rows / missing required columns exit 3; unparsable typed values exit 2.

+5. **Static type check** of the whole pipeline against the CSV schema (so type

+   errors surface even with zero rows) → exit 2.

+6. **Execute** row ops in order, then bucket by (window, group key), aggregate,

+   normalize, serialize. Runtime failures (division by zero, NaN/Inf) exit 4.

+

+All errors are raised as `MTLError(kind, msg)`; `main` prints exactly one line

+`ERROR:<kind>:<msg>` to STDERR and exits with the mapped code. Output is only

+written after full success.

+

+## DSL parsing

+

+* Lines are scanned with a quote-aware scanner: `#` outside a string starts a

+  comment. Physical lines are joined into one statement while brackets are

+  unbalanced or the text ends with `,` (this supports the multi-line

+  `aggregate` list).

+* Statements: `filter(expr)`, `apply(expr, ident)`, `group_by(ident | [ident,...])`,

+  `window(<int><m|h|d>)`, `aggregate fn(col|*) as alias, ...`.

+  Duplicate `group_by`/`window`, zero or multiple `aggregate`, unknown

+  statements, unknown aggregate functions, duplicate aliases, aliases colliding

+  with output keys → exit 1.

+* `filter`/`apply` run in declared order; `group_by`, `window`, `aggregate` are

+  declarative and act on the final row set (their position does not matter).

+* Expression grammar (recursive descent), lowest → highest precedence:

+  `|` → `&` → `!` → comparison / `in` (non-associative) → `+ -` → `* / %` →

+  unary `-` → primary (literal, column, `fn(args)`, `( expr )`).

+  Literals: `'string'` (no escapes; backslash rejected), ints, floats

+  (`1.`, `.5`, `1e3`), `true`/`false`.

+  Functions: `len`, `day`, `month`, `year`, `round(x[, digits])`.

+

+## Types

+

+`int`, `float` (both "numeric"), `str`, `bool`, `timestamp`.

+

+* Required columns: `timestamp`→timestamp, `price`/`quantity`→float, others str.

+* Extra columns are inferred over all non-empty values: int → float → bool

+  (`true`/`false`) → timestamp (must contain a time part) → str.

+* Empty cells in non-string columns are null. Nulls propagate through arithmetic

+  and transforms, make comparisons false, are skipped by aggregates (except

+  `count(*)`), and rows with a null `timestamp` are dropped from windowing.

+* Rules: arithmetic numeric-only (int op int → int, `/` → float); comparisons

+  numeric↔numeric, str↔str, timestamp↔timestamp, bool↔bool (`==`/`!=` only);

+  `&|!` bool-only; `in` only `'literal' in <str column>`; `filter` needs bool;

+  `len` str; `day/month/year` timestamp (evaluated in `--tz`); `round` numeric

+  with int digits; aggregates numeric only except `count(*)`; `window` needs

+  `timestamp` to be a timestamp column. Unknown columns are type errors.

+

+## Execution & output

+

+* Timestamps parsed with `--timestamp-format` (strptime) or ISO 8601

+  (`fromisoformat`, `Z` accepted); naive values localized to `--tz`, stored as

+  aware UTC datetimes.

+* Windows: tumbling, epoch-aligned, floor((t - epoch)/width) computed in integer

+  microseconds. Only non-empty windows are emitted.

+* Aggregates: sum (sequential), average = sum/n, median (mean of middle two

+  when even), population var (two-pass) and std = sqrt(var), min, max, count.

+  No input → `count` 0, others `null`. Any non-finite result → exit 4.

+* `round`: half away from zero via `Decimal(repr(x))` + `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

+* Row ordering: `window_start`, then group key tuple (nulls first, numbers

+  numeric, strings by code point, timestamps chronological).

+  Key order: `window_start`, `window_end`, group keys, aliases sorted.

+* Timestamps rendered `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]Z`. `-0.0` normalized to `0.0`.

+  JSON written with `indent=2`, `ensure_ascii=False`, trailing newline.
